structure.note: Two classes: each Class A Ordinary Share carries one vote; each Class B Ordinary Share carried 45 votes at January 31, 2026. Under the Shareholders' Deed and the Voting Proxy Deeds, co-founder Tan Hooi Ling, former President Maa Ming-Hokng and other executive officers irrevocably appoint Anthony Tan as proxy to vote their Class B shares, so the 20-F attributes 59.9% of total voting power to him (59.1% 'after giving effect to the Key Executive Proxies and Exco Proxies'), more than half. On March 24, 2026 shareholders approved new articles; the 20-F says the proposal raised each Class B share's votes from 45 to 90, which it said would give him about 74.9% of the voting power.

notes: All figures from Grab's FY2025 Form 20-F (fiscal year ended 31 December 2025; accession 0001855612-26-000020, filed March 6, 2026), read on sec.gov. USD throughout. OWNERSHIP (as stated, not recomputed): Anthony Tan, co-founder and CEO, 3.2% of total ordinary shares and 59.9% of voting power at January 31, 2026, on 3,972,725,983 Class A and 127,755,800 Class B shares. His 131,835,048 Class B shares include 81,099,260 he holds himself; 19,492,330 held by Hibiscus Worldwide Ltd.; 2,139,531 he may acquire within 60 days; 16,147,952 held by co-founder Tan Hooi Ling; 9,904,354 held by former President Maa Ming-Hokng and the Maa Trusts; and 3,051,621 held by or acquirable by other executive officers, all deemed beneficially owned by him under the Shareholders' Deed and Voting Proxy Deeds. The 3.2% therefore includes other people's shares that he votes, not only his own economic stake; no separate percentage for his own shares is given or derived. HOLDERS: SB Investment Advisers' 9.8% rests on a Form 13F filed February 18, 2026 (asOf is that filing date); Uber's rests on a Schedule 13D filed May 8, 2024 (asOf is that filing date); Toyota is dated as of the table. VOTING CHANGE: on March 24, 2026 an EGM approved new articles raising Class B votes from 45 to 90 per share (Form 6-K of March 24, 2026 and the 20-F's description of the proposal); the 59.9% predates it. DIVIDENDS: none. BUYBACKS: $274 million of Class A shares repurchased and retired in 2025, substantially completing the $500 million programme of February 2024; a new $500 million programme followed in February 2026 and a $750 million one in August 2026. STOCK COMP: $241 million equity-settled share-based payments. GEOGRAPHY: Note 19 of the financial statements by country; at two decimals in billions the segments sum to 3.39 against the stated total of 3.37 (US$3,370 million), a rounding difference only.

ecosystem.notes: The 20-F says GMV also includes "(i) sales made through offline stores reported under the deliveries segment; and (ii) revenues made from products and services provided to driver-partners, merchant-partners and other customers to support their businesses, such as GrabAds and GrabRentals". Grab reports GMV only for its on-demand businesses (deliveries 14,236 and mobility 7,901, in $ millions); it does not report financial services GMV. Total revenue (3,370) includes the financial services and others segments, which sit outside on-demand GMV, so Revenue / GMV slightly overstates the on-demand take. Deliveries revenue also includes supermarket sales (Jaya Grocer, and Everrise from March 2025). Revenue is after incentives: partner incentives were 1,002 and consumer incentives 1,268 in 2025. The 20-F reports no total paid out to drivers and merchants, so payouts is null.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Grab revenue includes financial services outside its on-demand GMV, so revenue ÷ GMV is not a like-for-like share.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F on sec.gov). IFRS, US$. Income tax paid is inside OCF; interest paid (26) is in financing and is added; interest received (171) is in investing, so it does not lower OCF. OCF (79) is depressed by the financial-services loan book growth (691 outflow), partly offset by banking-business customer deposits (308 inflow): flagged, not adjusted, and material (net −0.383bn vs paidOut 3.440bn). Revenue is after partner and consumer incentives (partner 1,002 and consumer 1,268 in 2025), so incentives paid to drivers and merchants are not in revenue or in paidOut; driver and merchant earnings in Grab's agent-model businesses are captured in salesEnabled instead. Lease principal (52) noted, not added.

marketcap.notes: Class A trades on Nasdaq as GRAB (directly, not as ADSs). Counts are from the third-quarter 2026 results release (furnished November 3, 2026), which states outstanding Class A and Class B ordinary shares of 3,942 million and 95 million at September 30, 2026, rounded to the nearest million. The interim report for the six months ended June 30, 2026 gives 3,973,517 thousand Class A and 117,785 thousand Class B in issue at June 30, 2026 (Class B including restricted shares not yet vested). Grab repurchased $400 million of shares in September and October 2026 and announced on September 15, 2026 that it intends to execute the remaining roughly $900 million of authorized repurchases over 12 months, so the edition-date count is likely lower. Warrants and the convertible notes are excluded.
